TODDLER ROOM LESSON · TODDLER ROOM · AGES 1–3 YEARS

Shoes — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches "shoes" at the door, where the word works: foot in, foot in, and the Velcro rip that is the toddler’s signature on getting dressed.

What is this?

Shoes are the blue-and-yellow sneakers that mean OUTSIDE — the most exciting dressing word in the language, because it always predicts adventure.

What does it mean?

The shoe word works because its reward never varies: shoes on, we go out. A word with a perfect track record gets believed — and said — early.

What does the child need to know?

You need the shoes, a sitting spot by the door and the ceremony: present each shoe, foot in, then hand over the Velcro. The rip is the child’s job; never do it for them.

Why this matters

Dressing battles shrink when the child owns the finisher. The Velcro rip is tiny, loud and theirs — the exact size of job that makes a two-year-old invincible.

What it teaches

Foot-eye coordination (the aim into the shoe), grip strength for the rip, left-right body awareness, and dressing-sequence pride.

Words to learn

shoesfootVelcroriponoutside

Say this to your child

“"Shoes! Where are your shoes? There they are! One foot — in! Other foot — push! Now YOUR job… rip the Velcro! RIIIIP! Shoes on… let’s go OUTSIDE!"”

Step by step

  1. By the door, the word: "shoes! Shoes on means we go OUT!"
  2. The ceremony: present the first shoe like a crown — "one foot… IN!"
  3. Second shoe, their push: "other foot… push… THERE!"
  4. Hand over the rip: "your job — rip the Velcro! RIIIIP!" Both shoes, both rips, both celebrations.
  5. Straight out the door: the word’s reward arrives on schedule, every time, which is why it never needs teaching twice.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "shoes" sits under a pair of blue and yellow sneakers — laced, waiting, facing the door.

Ask your child

"Where are your shoes?" "Which foot goes in first?" "Whose job is the Velcro?" (mine!)

What your child can say or do

Your child might say "shoes!" at the door, race to sit on the step, or rip the Velcro with a war cry — adventure, formally opened.

Out in the real world

Shoes live in racks, by doors, under beds — and on everyone else. "Look, daddy’s shoes! Baby’s shoes!" is a matching game the whole family plays.

Try it together

Shoe Shop: every shoe in the house on display, the toddler is the shopkeeper — "trying on" each pair (one foot only is fine), ripping every strap in stock. Fittings daily.

Understanding check

Ask: "What are these?" (shoes) "Where do feet go?" (in the shoes) "Whose job is the rip?" — name, aim, rip: out the door.

This lesson pairs with the Shoes flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Toddler Room.
